extracted.intended_audience: local journalists, newsroom leaders, media funders, policymakers, and others interested in news trust and local journalism
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and measures to assess how much local news is trusted and how well local news outlets perform core civic functions (coverage usefulness, bias, accountability, transparency, and community impact).

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall public trust level (local vs national)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure of how much Americans trust reporting by local news organizations versus national news organizations (45% trust local reporting “a great deal” or “quite a lot,” compared to 31% for national).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as a headline metric to compare relative trust; track changes over time to detect erosion. The article emphasizes that local trust currently outperforms national but is fragile.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accomplishing key tasks of informing communities
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether local news organizations are accomplishing the key tasks of informing communities (six in 10 Americans believe local outlets accomplish most key tasks).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate performance against a list of community-informing tasks (public information, local event coverage, issue explanation). This is a broad evaluative dimension capturing core mission fulfillment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perceived caring, trustworthiness, and neutrality of journalists
rubrics_metrics.description: Public perceptions of local journalists as caring (36%), trustworthy (29%), and neutral or unbiased (23%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure audience attitudes toward reporters themselves, not just content; these perceptions influence overall trust and can be improved via transparency and engagement practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Usefulness of coverage for daily life
rubrics_metrics.description: Extent to which local news covers issues Americans can use in their daily life (79% say local news is better than national at this).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess beat and service journalism that helps residents navigate daily needs (schools, public works, health services); prioritize practical reporting that residents find immediately relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perceived impartiality / reporting without bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Share of the public who feel local reporting is done without bias (66% reported this).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track perceptions of bias separately from ideological labeling; perceived impartiality supports trust and can be undermined by partisan framing of stories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relative confidence compared to other local institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Public confidence in local news compared with other local institutions (only local government ranks lower: 37% trust local news a great deal/quite a lot vs 73% for libraries and 56% for law enforcement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use comparative benchmarking to understand the standing of local news in the civic ecosystem; low comparative trust signals need for reputation-building and community engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partisan polarization of trust
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree to which a person’s political affiliation determines confidence in local news (50% of Democrats express confidence vs 27% of Republicans — a 23-point gap).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor differences in trust by political affiliation and consider strategies to reach across partisan divides; recognize that national-level polarization is filtering down locally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perceived ideological slant of local news
rubrics_metrics.description: Public view of whether local news is ideologically balanced: 53% say 'about right,' 26% 'too liberal,' and 15% 'too conservative.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use audience perception surveys to assess ideological balance; address perceptions through clear sourcing, context, and transparent editorial standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effectiveness of accountability reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether local news is holding powerful people and institutions accountable (60% feel local news does only a 'fair' or 'poor' job on accountability reporting).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat investigative and watchdog reporting as a specific performance area to strengthen. The study flags accountability reporting as an area needing improvement and a core civic function.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic coverage gaps and priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Extent to which local outlets cover topics the public wants more of (areas cited needing more attention: drug addiction 65%; K–12 education 64%; the environment 64%; plans for public works projects 64%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use audience-identified topic priorities to guide resource allocation and beat coverage; tracking topical coverage gaps can improve perceived usefulness and relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency around sources and reporters’ backgrounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Transparency practices regarding sources, reporters’ backgrounds, and how stories are reported (initiatives supported to promote more transparency).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt and publicize transparent sourcing, reporter bios, and methods to build trust. Knight-supported initiatives are cited as examples to increase confidence in media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local focus versus national coverage choices
rubrics_metrics.description: Decision to emphasize local reporting instead of providing national coverage, especially when resources are scarce (the study advises local outlets should continue to focus on the local).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize local beats and issues that differentiate local outlets from national media; avoiding duplicative national coverage may preserve the outlet’s distinct value and trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact on civic life and democratic participation
rubrics_metrics.description: The role of local news in supporting civic health — without coverage, fewer people run for office, vote, or become involved in communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use measures of civic engagement (candidate emergence, turnout, community involvement) as downstream indicators of local news value; frame reporting priorities to support civic participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial sustainability and demonstrated value
rubrics_metrics.description: The uncertain financial future of local news and the need to demonstrate the value local news organizations provide (a forthcoming Knight study will focus on value and financial outlook).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess business model viability and communicate impact/value to funders and the public; financial health affects capacity to sustain accountability and beats that build trust.
